title: Onboarding orientation: Nexa Health procurement, SLA, billing & escrow
next_steps: Jordan to send redlined MSA draft with proposed data residency clause by 2026-06-04
Mira to run 48-hour latency/cost benchmark on customer-supplied prompt set and share spreadsheet by 2026-06-07
Sam to schedule security deep-dive with Infosec (SOC2 + KMS) for week of 2026-06-08
Carlos to provide procurement scoring matrix and target deployment date (goal: 2026-07-15)
action_items: Jordan: circulate MSA + DPA redlines (include escrow billing flow) - due 2026-06-04
Mira: bench run + detailed cost/latency sheet - due 2026-06-07
Sam: set up Infosec review meeting and share SOC2 artifact link - due 2026-06-09
Anika: provide list of mandatory contract clauses (data residency, audit rights) - due 2026-06-03
summary: Procurement and legal orientation covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, billing cadence and escrow options. Customer emphasized data residency and audit/KMS requirements; pricing needs approval through finance committee. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs dedicated options, fallback policies, and proposed pilot acceptance criteria.
topics: Billing cycles, invoicing, and escrow flow
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: okay thanks everybody for joining uh, this is Jordan from Redwood, um, we brought Mira and Sam on for technical and cs. uh quick roll call?
00:22 Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, procurement, afternoon all.
00:27 Anika Bose: Anika from legal on my end.
00:30 Tom Whitman: Tom, CTO. Priya is on but muted.
00:35 Priya Kapoor: (muted) yes hi, Priya.
00:40 Jordan Patel: Great, high level for today's call — align on the MSA/DPA path, SLA tiers, billing cadence, and then next steps for a short pilot. does that sound right Tom/Carlos?
00:55 Tom Whitman: Yep, that covers it. We're mainly trying to close procurement gating items this week.
01:05 Mira Chen: Quick note — we heard data residency and KMS were must-haves, we'll outline options: hosted with region pinning, Dedicated, or Private (VPC).
01:18 Carlos Rivera: Exactly. Our risk team flagged two things: explicit data residency in the contract, and escrow for pre-paid credits. Also, invoicing needs to align with our monthly net-45 processing.
01:34 Jordan Patel: Understood. On escrow — can you clarify whether you mean a third-party escrow account for prepayments, or more like a retained balance with us?
01:42 Carlos Rivera: Third-party escrow — legal prefers independent custody for the initial committed spend during pilot.
01:48 Anika Bose: And we need audit rights on logs, and proof of key management, so KMS integration details are important.
01:55 Sam Ortiz: Noted. We can provide KMS integration docs and HSM attestations. On audit logs, we have per-request logging with TTL options, and we can provide export to your SIEM.
02:06 Anika Bose: Also want a sample DPA with subprocessor list, and an explicit clause about not using customer data for model training.
02:15 Mira Chen: We do not train on customer data; we can add that explicit statement. DPA includes subprocessor list as an attachment — it is periodically updated.
02:25 Carlos Rivera: Great. Pricing side — Priya, do you want to weigh in?
02:30 Priya Kapoor: Yes, our finance team will need a fixed monthly commit number for the budget. We also need unit pricing for overages and a forecast of expected monthly spend if the pilot scales. Net-45 is a must.
02:44 Jordan Patel: We typically offer usage-based billing for hosted with invoice monthly; reserved capacity (Dedicated) can be invoiced monthly or as annual commit. We can accommodate net-45, but need to confirm the billing owner and tax details in the MSA.
02:58 Tom Whitman: For SLA, our app depends on low tail latency. We need to understand latency SLOs, SLO crediting, and multi-region failover.
03:10 Mira Chen: On latency, our profiles show p95 under 250ms for small requests on Dedicated in region, hosted varies by load. We can propose an SLA matrix: bronze/silver/gold tiers with corresponding uptime and latency commitments and credits.
03:27 Carlos Rivera: Can you put exact credit math in the MSA? Procurement needs a formula.
03:32 Jordan Patel: Yes — we'll include explicit credit calculation and claim process (ticketing, 30-day claim window).
03:40 Anika Bose: For DPA, we need to ensure deletion/return procedures are clear, and retention windows documented for logs and prompts. Also, incident notification windows need to be contractual.
03:51 Sam Ortiz: Incident notification is 24 hours for severity 1 by default for enterprise plans, and we'll include extended forensic support for Dedicated/Private.
04:02 Carlos Rivera: On the escrow flow, how would refunds or dispute resolution work?
04:10 Jordan Patel: Typical approach: escrow holds committed funds; billing draws are reconciled monthly; unused committed funds can be refunded at end of term minus usage. We can document dispute resolution and clawback terms.
04:22 Anika Bose: We may need a clause for early termination and exit assistance, with data handoff procedures and certified deletion.
04:30 Mira Chen: We'll include an exit plan with exported data format (JSON NDJSON) and a certified deletion affidavit.
04:38 Tom Whitman: Security artifacts — can you share your latest SOC2 Type II report and any penetration test summaries?
04:45 Sam Ortiz: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and the last external pentest summary. We can also set up a direct SFTP for artifact delivery to your legal team.
04:56 Priya Kapoor: For purchasing approval, our finance committee requires a cost/benefit one-pager comparing Redwood to in-house and to Anthropic. Can you help with a short TCO comparison?
05:09 Jordan Patel: Absolutely. Mira, we should prepare a TCO with expected token volumes, latency trade-offs, and Dedicated vs hosted assumptions.
05:17 Mira Chen: I'll run a benchmark using their sample prompt set — it'll show cost per 1k tokens and p95 latency.
05:24 Carlos Rivera: We'll need that before the procurement committee meets on 06/10.
05:30 Jordan Patel: Okay target dates: MSA redlines by 06/04; benchmark sheet by 06/07 to allow time before 06/10.
05:38 Anika Bose: One more legal nuance — we have an internal clause on 'data residency exception process' where certain teams can approve temporary cross-region processing for specific endpoints. Can you support ad-hoc exceptions?
05:52 Mira Chen: We can support exceptions with documented approvals and an access log for each exception. We'll need to codify the approval workflow.
05:59 Carlos Rivera: Good. On SLA caps — is there a maximum aggregate credit? Procurement often won't accept uncapped liability but we want meaningful credits.
06:10 Jordan Patel: Standard is a cap equal to monthly invoice for that service, but we can discuss negotiated higher caps for enterprise contracts. We'll flag that as a negotiation point.
06:21 Tom Whitman: About private deployment: if we go Private (VPC/on-prem) what's the timeline for deployment and support?
06:30 Mira Chen: VPC deploy typically 6–8 weeks for network prep and validation, on-prem can be 10–12 weeks depending on hardware procurement. We'll map tasks and deliverables in an onboarding plan.
06:42 Priya Kapoor: For finance — can you support an escrow vs monthly invoice hybrid during pilot? We want initial escrow deposit but then monthly reconciled billing.
06:52 Jordan Patel: Yes, hybrid is common. We'll draft language: initial escrow deposit to guarantee pilot capacity, then monthly reconciliations with net-45 invoices for overages.
07:01 Anika Bose: One detail — we require subprocessor notification 30 days before changes; can you commit to a minimum notice period?
07:09 Sam Ortiz: We provide 30-day notice for major subprocessor changes; for urgent security patches we might do shorter notification but will follow up.
07:18 Carlos Rivera: Good. On the acceptance criteria for pilot — we need test cases, SLO verification, and a runbook for failure modes.
07:28 Mira Chen: We'll propose a 4-week pilot acceptance plan: week 0 onboarding + integration, week 1 baseline tests, week 2 load test and latency verification, week 3 customer sign-off. Acceptance criteria will include p95 latency < X ms, error rate < 0.5%, and data residency compliance.
07:44 Tom Whitman: We also want a rollback plan if model quality regresses; how do rollouts work?
07:52 Mira Chen: Rollouts are controlled — canary and automatic fallback to previous model variant; we'll include rollback SLAs in the operational annex.
08:02 Jordan Patel: Let's talk specific contract language around training and IP — Anika, you asked about no training on customer data. We will add explicit non-training clause, along with a warranty.
08:14 Anika Bose: We'll also want indemnification language for data breaches arising from Redwood's negligence.
08:21 Jordan Patel: Standard indemnities apply; we'll share our MSA which contains indemnification and limitation language for negotiation.
08:29 Priya Kapoor: For the procurement scoring, please include reliability and cost as weighted factors — our IT team will provide weights.
08:36 Carlos Rivera: Also include transition assistance fees and estimated cost of switching back if we choose to leave.
08:43 Mira Chen: We'll include estimated export bandwidth and time to export for large datasets.
08:49 Jordan Patel: Okay I think we're converging. Quick recap — Jordan to send MSA draft w/ DPA redlines including escrow clause by 06/04; Mira to run benchmark using provided prompt set and share cost/latency spreadsheet by 06/07; Sam to schedule SOC2 + KMS deep-dive with Infosec week of 06/08; customer will share procurement matrix and mandatory clauses by 06/03. Any other immediate items?
09:12 Carlos Rivera: Please include example SLA credit math in the MSA, and a pilot SOW template.
09:20 Jordan Patel: Noted. We'll include both.
09:25 Tom Whitman: One off question — is there a way to escrow encryption keys separately? We don't want provider-controlled keys for some workloads.
09:34 Sam Ortiz: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Dedicated/Private. For hosted, bring-your-own-key (BYOK) is possible with specific integrations, we'll detail options.
09:44 Anika Bose: Okay thanks. We'll review docs when you send.
09:47 Jordan Patel: Great. We'll follow up with attachments and set the security deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
09:55 (end of recorded portion — remaining discussion was off the record logistics)
notes: Shared links referenced: MSA draft (link to be sent), SOC2 Type II artifact (link to be sent), benchmark spreadsheet template (to be provided by Mira)
Customer timeline: procurement committee meeting on 2026-06-10; target go-live window mid-July 2026
Tone: constructive; main sticking points = escrow flow, explicit data residency clause, SLA credit caps
